$comment: Citations an audit read against the row's own action text and judged do NOT support it. Consumed by `yarn validate:anatomy-keyboard` (see `RejectedCitation` in anatomy-keyboard.ts). A rejected citation is skipped and the walk keeps going -- to the next line of the same file, then the next route -- so the row lands on a better owner or on none. This file can therefore only ever make `backed` FALL, never rise, which is what makes it safe to check in. RULE, and it is a ceiling's rule: an entry may be ADDED by any audit; an entry may be REMOVED only when the row is re-cited to a site that is not the rejected one, or the row is withdrawn. Deleting an entry to recover a `backed` count is the same act as raising a ceiling. Seeded by RESIDUAL-14, whose census adjudicated all 404 rows against their 220 citation sites: 352 genuine, 52 naming a real file for the wrong claim, 0 undecidable. 31 of the 52 are caught structurally instead -- comment-stripping, the `modifiers` rule, the dynamic-component rule, the boundary-free handler token -- or are fixed by correcting a wrong row, and are NOT listed here. What is listed is the residue: a real handler or a real element, correctly reached, doing something other than what the row's sentence says. That is the one thing a checker cannot decide for itself, and RESIDUAL-05 drew the same line when it said an import proves a component is loaded and not that the spec asserts anything about it.

D-RES14-2, IMPLEMENTED by RESIDUAL-15 -- this entry was WIDENED-then-NARROWED rather than deleted. RESIDUAL-14 wrote it as `DzTransfer.vue:*` (every line) because the only thing in the file that named a printable character was the pane's `searchable` text `<input>`, a field that FILTERS rather than moving focus among options, and `templateNodesIn` printed a template-body offset for it so no single line could be named. RESIDUAL-15 gave the pane a real `typeAheadIndex` reading each rendered option's own `textContent`, so the row is now owned by `onPaneKeydown`'s `default:` arm under route `own`. The entry stays, narrowed to the two lines the source and target panes' search `<input>` elements sit on (`:414`, `:530`), because those nodes still do not back this row and the ledger ratchets: removing the `:*` widening is what the re-citation earns, and deleting the entry is not. Route `own` is asked before `platform`, so the entry is now inert -- which is the point: it is a guard against the citation coming back, not a subtraction.
